subject: Exec Weekly: priorities, QBR readout plan, wins/risks/asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec Weekly snapshot — priorities, QBR readout plan, wins/risks/asks

Team — sending a compact weekly snapshot to align on QBR readiness and a couple of asks ahead of Tuesday’s leadership readout. I’ve attached a working deck (QBR_readout_slide_v1.pdf) — please review slides 2–6 (priorities + 2 customer callouts). High level below.

Wins
- Hosted API latency improvements: infra pushed model caching tweak reduced 95th pct latency by ~18% for typical 1–2k token calls (release in staging; soak looks good). Owner: Markus.
- Two Design Engineers onboarded to Platform DX; ramp timeline shortened to 4 weeks vs 6. Owner: Grace.
- Acme POC completed initial security review; SOC artifacts delivered (Sarah confirmed receipt).

Risks / open blockers
- Acme procurement: legal flagged an SLA exception request for data retention terms that may require an escalation. (Risk to closed-won timing). Owner: Laura.
- QBR narrative: we currently lack a single ‘efficiency story’ slide tying batch/caching improvements to unit cost — need a concise metric and chart. Owner: Markus + Marissa.

Asks (concrete)
1) Markus: please add a one-slide cost delta (before/after caching) + a short 1–2 bullet explanation for execs by EOD Monday (2027-04-05 18:00 PDT).
2) Laura: can you summarize the SLA exception ask and one proposed mitigation (slide or note) and loop procurement contacts? We need wording suitable for execs.
3) Vivek/Grace: any critical headcount or resourcing asks to surface in QBR? If yes, send 1-line justification by Monday noon.

Attachments: QBR_readout_slide_v1.pdf (application/pdf) — working draft; Acme_SLA_exception_notes.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks — brief replies only please so I can consolidate into the master deck.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec Weekly snapshot — priorities, QBR readout plan, wins/risks/asks

Sounds good — I can take the cost slide. Quick clarification: for the cost delta, do you want token-level unit cost (per-1k tokens) or a customer-facing cost-per-session example? I can do both but will need to compress to a single chart.

Also, should I add a one-line note on expected uplift next quarter from the new batching heuristics? That helps tie to roadmap.

— Markus
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec Weekly snapshot — priorities, QBR readout plan, wins/risks/asks

Marissa — looping Sarah from Acme so we can confirm procurement timeline and whether the SLA exception is a blocker for signing. Sarah, can you confirm whether procurement needs an approved exception before the CFO signs off, or if we can route the exception post-signature with a milestone?

Markus — token-level unit cost + one customer-facing session example is ideal; put the two numbers side-by-side and then a single chart showing percent delta. Keep the text to 1–2 bullets.

I’ll draft a short mitigation note for the SLA exception (one paragraph + proposed 60-day technical mitigation) and share the doc by Monday morning.

— Laura
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@acme.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec Weekly snapshot — priorities, QBR readout plan, wins/risks/asks

Thanks for the ping, Laura. Quick update from Acme procurement: the team prefers to have the SLA exception language settled prior to the CFO signature for enterprise deals of this size. That said, we are amenable to an interim milestone plan if Redwood provides a signed commitment to implement the mitigation within 60 days and acceptable reporting. I’ve attached the procurement intake note (summary below).

Key points:
- Preferred path: SLA exception approved by procurement/legal prior to signature.
- Alternate: conditional signature if a 60-day mitigation plan + weekly reporting is attached to the contract.
- Timeline: procurement review complete by 2027-04-12 if we deliver final language by EOD 2027-04-06.

We’re aiming to avoid delaying the signature but need clear contractual language. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

— Sarah Lin
Director of IT Procurement, Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec Weekly snapshot — priorities, QBR readout plan, wins/risks/asks

Thanks, all — short turnaround plan:
1) Markus: please upload the cost slide to the Drive link and point to the exact chart I should pull for slides by 18:00 PDT Monday.
2) Laura: appreciate the mitigation paragraph — please drop it into Acme_SLA_exception_notes.docx and I’ll extract 1–2 bullets for slide 5.
3) Sarah/Procurement: noted on timeline — we’ll aim to provide final language by EOD 2027-04-06 to hit your review window. Marissa will coordinate legal.

I’ll merge inputs and circulate a final handout for the Tuesday readout (leadership distro) by Monday 20:00 PDT. If anyone has a blocker to those deadlines, ping me directly.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR_PREP_LINK
HubSpot: HS-4321

— Marissa
VP, Customer Success & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
